While I personally think that immigrants most likely have increased the number of rapes in Sweden, I think people should consider that the statistics on rape in Sweden is a little bit misleading at a first glance.

First of all, there was a reform in sex crime legislation in 2005 which made the legal definition of rape much broader than before: "The change in law meant that cases where the victim was asleep or intoxicated are now included in the figures. Previously they'd been recorded as another category of crime." Raping drunk people wasn't considered rape before, and therefor weren't included in the infamous Swedish rape statistics. Not to mention there has been a lot of campaigns to spread awareness about rape the last decade, so more people have been coming forward than usual. Keep this in mind.

Sweden is always considered to have the highest acts of rape on the whole world, but also consider the fact that 63 countries out in the world doesn't even record rape. In a lot of countries out there men and women are still afraid to come forward after rape, and often feel too ashamed to. Again, in Sweden there has been a lot of awareness taking place, urging people to come forward. Sweden is even ahead of most countries in opening male rape clinics and spreading the word that guys can actually be raped too (even if that concept, by general consensus even in Sweden, is still considered taboo and something that doesn't happen).

Unlike other countries, Sweden collects its crime data when the offense in question is carried out. So even if it was later proven that no rape took place, it still retains this classification in the published crime statistics.

Last, but not least, I want you all to consider the fact that Sweden records each act of rape separately; if the same person reports that he/she has been raped several times, each and every one of those times are counted. It basically means that if a person says that he or she was raped by his or her spouse everyday for a year, 365 acts of rapes are entered into the Swedish crime statistics. This is super important to remember.

So, in 2014 there were 6,700 reported cases of rape, a number that has interestingly stayed relatively unchanged since 2005 when there was a new sex act legislation put into law (meaning that more acts was considered rape than before), and if we also keep in mind that rapes are still recorded to the crime statistics whether it was proven false or not (do women ever lie about rape? Certainly seems to be a popular opinion on here - and not necessarily an untrue one, although I should say people, and not only women), and don't forget that 10 people report that they've been raped every day of the year - again, whether it's true or not - can literally make up almost *half of Sweden's rape reports this year.
